analysis: Both changed files are documentation only: changelog.d/coordinator-traffic-verdict.md (head lines 3-6) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (the `Traffic:` bullet of the status section, head lines 1045-1062 per the range map). No executable code, auth, crypto, key-handling, or protocol logic is touched, so no direct regression is possible from these edits. The docs describe provider diagnostics and re-registration behavior. The new semantics: status judged from current evidence only; a refusal counts if it is at most 60s old (`refusalMaxAge`) and not within the first 90s after connecting (`statusGraceSeconds`); older refusals read `unconfirmed` with no fix; a routed request after the latest status reads as eligible; a new `coordinator_connection.last_request_at` state field; re-registration is triggered only by a persistent current refusal, not by a refusal sent once at registration, and waits for provider idle. Threat relevance: TB-011 and T-052/T-053 (stale vs current authorization), T-057 (availability), TB-002. The docs say the Traffic line is diagnostic and grants no serving authorization. They say re-registration only starts a fresh coordinator verification session, so authorization stays coordinator-owned. The docs also say legacy-verified Macs get no status after the registration-time refusal. This is an unverified coordinator-behavior contract, consistent with the platform-owned backend scope, so it is not evidence of a regression. Limits: the Swift implementation (StatusCommand, ProviderLoop re-registration, state-file writer) is not in the supplied evidence. A later pass should check three things. First, that treating a routed request as eligible evidence cannot make local status or re-registration logic override coordinator/App Attest authorization (T-052/T-053). Second, that the unconditional re-registration timer cannot be driven by coordinator or consumer input into a reconnect storm (T-057). Third, that `last_request_at` in the state file leaks nothing sensitive (T-058); it is a timestamp only.
